episodes.166605: Severe thunderstorms moved across Houston counties and produced some wind damage.
episodes.166618: A deep trough over the Midwest and a moist, buoyant warm sector over the region led to a line of strong storms over southern central Indiana by the early evening.  As a squall line organized and enveloped downstream cells, the resulting bowing segments led to damaging winds and broad rotation in a bookend vortex radar signature.  Straight line wind damage occurred along the path of the bowing segment, with significant damage to boat docks on Lake Monroe in Monroe County, as well as the Country Squire Lakes trailer park in Jennings County.  The region of broad rotation eventually lead to a brief tornado in south-central Decatur County.
episodes.166690: There were several lines of strong to occasionally severe thunderstorms that moved northward across southern Minnesota, and into portions of central Minnesota, and west central Wisconsin. The largest hail stones occurred in far southern Minnesota where deep layer shear and ample instability existed. Some of the largest hailstones occurred near Mankato, and south of Mankato toward the Iowa border, where there were a few reports of measured golf ball and half dollar size hail.  There were also numerous reports of smaller hail stones across southern Minnesota.
episodes.167203: Isolated thunderstorms developed in a strong southerly wind flow ahead of a cold front over Missouri. One of the storms produced nickel-size hail.
episodes.167205: A squall line of thunderstorms occurred ahead of a strong cold front that trailed southward from a low pressure center over the Great Lakes region. The squall line moved rapidly east-northeast from Arkansas and northwest Tennessee across southwest Kentucky. Pockets of minor to moderate wind damage occurred south of a line from Paducah to Madisonville to Owensboro. A few brief tornadoes accompanied meso-vortices within the line. Heavy rainfall associated with this system caused minor flooding on the Green River, along with a few flooded roads.
episodes.167332: An ice jam developed on the Saint John River...in the vicinity of Dickey...during the evening of the 12th. Rising river levels led to flooding and the closure of a portion of Route 161...near the Allagash and Saint Francis town line. The road closure was brief. The waters also reached the first floor of one camp...with water also in the basement of another house. The ice jam released and moved around 90 minutes later allowing river levels to fall and allowing the road to re-open once ice was cleared from the road. This evolved into an ice flow which grew to around 9 miles in length. The ice flow occasionally jammed while moving downriver through the morning of the 16th. However...flooding with these additional ice jams was generally minor mostly impacting low lying agricultural flood plain areas. Locations which experienced this minor lowland flooding extended from Allagash...to Fort Kent...to Madawaska...to Van Buren and Hamlin. The ice flow cleared the region during the morning of the 16th.
episodes.167333: An ice jam developed on the Little Black River during the afternoon of the 13th and persisted into the early morning hours of the 15th. Water levels rose upriver from the jam. The rising waters led to minor flooding along portions of Walker Brook Road...Rapid Road and Little Black Road. The flooding also impacted several homes and structures along the river. The ice jam released during the early morning hours of the 15th allowing river levels to fall.
episodes.167546: Scattered thunderstorms moved across parts of northern Illinois during the afternoon of April 13th, which caused localized wind damage.
episodes.167547: Scattered thunderstorms moved across parts of southern Lake Michigan during the afternoon of April 13th.
episodes.167604: A large upper trough dug through the Southern Plains during the afternoon and overnight hours on April 12th-13th, allowing the dry line to mix east into Central Texas. Large scale forcing increased along the dry line across Central Texas during the late afternoon through the evening, as these storms tapped moderate instability and increasing wind shear ahead of this system. These storms eventually developed in a quasi-linear convection system (QLCS), as they became severe and accelerated east across much of East Texas during the evening through the early morning hours of the 13th. Instances of large hail and damaging winds were reported from these storms, before they moved into North Louisiana during the early morning hours. The southern extent of this complex of storms eventually slowed as they became more parallel (west to east) to the extensive area of damaging winds, resulting in these storms developing/moving repeatedly over the same areas of Nacogdoches and Shelby Counties. Thus, instances of flash flooding were reported across these areas, as widespread rainfall amounts of three to in excess of five inches were observed. Additional showers and thunderstorms developed across East Texas during the mid-morning through the early afternoon hours of April 13th along a cold front, with some of these storms also becoming severe, downing trees across the area. These storms exited East Texas into Southwest Arkansas and North Louisiana during the early afternoon hours.
episodes.167611: A shortwave moved into the Lower Mississippi Valley triggering numerous showers and thunderstorms across Arkansas during the morning hours of April 13, 2022. Storms eventually organized into a line that swept across the Mid-South. A strong low-level jet, large amounts of wind shear, and moderate amounts of instability supported severe thunderstorms across the Mid-South. Large hail, damaging wind and tornadoes were the result. Locally heavy rain also caused flooding.

episodes.167639: A large upper trough dug through the Southern Plains during the afternoon and overnight hours on April 12th-13th, allowing the dry line to mix east into Central Texas. Large scale forcing increased along the dry line across Central Texas during the late afternoon through the evening, as these storms tapped moderate instability and increasing wind shear ahead of this system. In fact, isolated showers and a few thunderstorms developed during the mid and late afternoon across portions of Northeast Louisiana, with one storm spawning a brief tornado over Northeast Ouachita Parish near the Swartz community. These storms over Central Texas eventually developed in a quasi-linear convection system (QLCS), as they became severe and accelerated east across much of East Texas and North Louisiana during the evening through the early morning hours of the 12th-13th. Instances of damaging winds were reported from these storms, downing numerous trees and power lines, and even spawning isolated tornadoes as well. While these storms exited the region prior to daybreak on the 13th, additional showers and thunderstorms developed along the associated cold front across East Texas during the mid and late morning of the 13th, before spreading into North Louisiana during the peak heating of the afternoon. Thus, adequate instability developed such that some of these storms again became severe, producing instances of damaging winds over portions of North Louisiana and an isolated tornado over Eastern Winn/Western Caldwell Parishes. These storms finally exited North Louisiana during the late afternoon hours of the 13th.
episodes.167723: A large upper trough dug through the Southern Plains during the afternoon and overnight hours on April 12th-13th, allowing the dry line to mix east into Central Texas. Large scale forcing increased along the dry line across Central Texas during the late afternoon through the evening, as these storms tapped moderate instability and increasing wind shear ahead of this system. These storms over Central Texas eventually developed in a quasi-linear convection system (QLCS), as they became severe and accelerated east across much of East Texas, North Louisiana, and portions of Southern Arkansas during the evening through the early morning hours of the 12th-13th. Instances of damaging winds were reported from these storms in Southwest Arkansas, downing multiple trees, and even spawning an isolated tornado near Prescott in Nevada County. These storms exited Southern Arkansas just prior to midnight on the 13th. Additional scattered strong to severe thunderstorms redeveloped over Northeast Texas and Southeast Oklahoma after daybreak on the 13th ahead of a cold front, and spread east into Southwest Arkansas during the mid-morning hours. Some of these storms produced damaging winds which downed trees across portions of Southwest Arkansas before shifting east out the area by mid-afternoon.
episodes.167833: A strong storm system brought multiple rounds of severe weather that led to fairly widespread rainfall and eventually river flooding. One round of severe weather occurred on Monday, April 11th. Large, individual thunderstorms known as supercells developed along the Arkansas River valley of western Arkansas. As these storms slowly drifted east, they produced four tornadoes across Sebastian, Franklin and Logan Counties and hail as large as 4.5 in diameter across Logan County. Later in the evening, storms began to develop across central Arkansas and move generally eastward. Two storms caused the most widespread severe weather across central into eastern Arkansas during the evening hours of the 11th. The main storm of interest developed across Perry and Faulkner Counties and moved east southeastward toward Lonoke County. As this storm intensified it produced a tornado as well as 3 hail near Cabot. The other main storm developed over portions of Garland County and moved east across Saline County. Before weakening, it produced a swath of hail as large as golf balls from Hot Springs Village to Bryant. ||Ahead of a cold front that moved across the state on the 13th, additional rain and thunderstorms developed and moved across the state. Fairly widespread rain, some of which was heavy and led to flash flooding, and thunderstorms shifted east across the area on the 13th. A swath of heavy rain in excess of 2-4 inches occurred from portions of southwest to east central Arkansas as well as across northwest sections of the state. Sadly, one person died after a tree fell on a mobile home in Cleveland County on April 13th. On the same day, flash flooding claimed the life of a 70 year old woman in Carroll County when she attempted to cross a flooded low water crossing.
episodes.167941: Initial storms developed within the warm sector of a surface low that tracked northwest of the area, followed by a strong cold front with associated dry line that produced a quasi-linear (QLCS) storm mode later in the evening. Several tornadoes occurred across western into northern Iowa.  Initially the tornadoes were associated with supercell storms, however later storms produced QLCS tornadoes as it raced east northeast across the state. In addition to the tornadoes, hail up to tennis ball size occurred with initial super cells. The later QLCS produced hail up to golf ball sized along with damaging wind gusts over 70 mph at times.||Additionally, total rainfall in excess of 2 to 4 inches fell in a swath across areas that dealt with the severe thunderstorm and tornado warnings earlier in the event. While no flash flooding was experienced, rainfall in the Winnebago River basin above Mason City resulted in minor river flooding on April 13th, exceeding minor flood stage in the morning and receding below flood stage that evening.
episodes.168097: A deepening midlevel trough over the central Rockies advected north an unstable airmass into Nebraska and Iowa. Storms initiated to the northeast of the triple point leading to two tornadoes and numerous hail and strong wind gusts.
episodes.168098: A deepening midlevel trough over the central Rockies advected north an unstable airmass into Nebraska and Iowa. Storms initiated to the northeast of the triple point leading to two tornadoes and numerous hail and strong wind gusts.
episodes.168141: A line of strong to severe thunderstorms moved through eastern Oklahoma during the morning hours of the 13th, ahead of a cold front that moved through the area. Wind damage occurred with the stronger storms within the line. Very strong low level wind shear combined with marginally strong instability to result in a few strong low level circulations along the leading edge of the line of thunderstorms as it moved eastward. One such circulation produced a tornado in Adair County.
episodes.168142: A line of thunderstorms developed into northwestern Arkansas during the morning of the 13th, as a cold front moved into the area. A strong thunderstorm within the line produced hail up to nickel size. More impactfully, this line of showers and thunderstorms was slow-moving, with individual cells within the line moving northeasterly repeatedly across the same areas, which resulted in locally heavy rainfall. Two to four inches of rain occurred locally, which subsequently resulted in flash flooding across portions of Benton, Washington, Carroll, and Madison Counties. After the rainfall had ended, some low water crossings remained flooded for hours, and a woman drowned when she attempted to drive through one of these low water crossings in Carroll County.
episodes.168167: A squall line developed during the evening hours of 4/12 and primarily produced large hail. There was one report of a severe wind gust.
episodes.168211: Two rounds of severe storms moved across southeast Minnesota on April 12th. The first round occurred in the afternoon as storms producing large hail moved across the area. Quarter sized hail fell from north of Racine (Mower County) east to near Winona (Winona County). A second round of severe storms occurred in the evening. An EF2 tornado moved through Taopi (Mower County), where homes were destroyed or severely damaged, grain bins were destroyed, cars were tossed or rolled, and trees and power lines were downed. Two people sustained injuries while sheltering from the storm when they became trapped under debris. An EF1 tornado occurred just southwest of Spring Valley (Fillmore County), damaging several farm outbuildings and trees. Two EF0 tornadoes occurred southwest of Lewiston (Winona County), where the damage was mainly to trees and one farm. The Mower County Board of Commissioners ratified an emergency declaration for Taopi and a state of emergency was declared for Fillmore County.
episodes.168213: Two rounds of severe storms moved across western Wisconsin on April 12th. The first round occurred in the afternoon as storms producing large hail moved across the area. Quarter to walnut sized hail fell from Galesville (Trempealeau County) east to New Rome (Adams County). The second round occurred in the evening as more severe storms moved through. These storms blew the roof off a barn near Tomah (Monroe County).
episodes.168215: Severe storms moved across northeast Iowa during the evening of April 12th. These storms produced five tornadoes and damaging wind gusts as high as 72 mph in Nora Springs (Floyd County). EF1 tornadoes occurred near Brownville (Mitchell County) and south of Riceville in both Mitchell and Howard Counties with both tornadoes damaging farm buildings and trees. EF0 tornadoes touched down in northern Floyd County into southern Mitchell County west of Orchard, near Saratoga (Howard County), and close to Ridgeway (Winneshiek County) with damage limited to trees and a few farm buildings. The Governor of Iowa issued a disaster proclamation for Howard, Mitchell, and Winneshiek Counties.
episodes.168283: Another round of storms with heavy rainfall moved into the region ahead of a cold front from the early morning through the early afternoon hours. The most notable flooding occurred at Roaring River State Park, where over three inches of rain caused the Roaring River to rise over 6 feet within a two-hour period. Evacuations were conducted with over 30 people moved from the campground near the river. Other reports of flooding were received along and south of interstate 44 where numerous low water crossings flooded. Most of the flood reports were received from areas where over two inches of rain fell during this event.
episodes.168378: A strong low pressure system resulted in a northward push of warmth and moisture into the mid-upper Missouri River Basin during the late afternoon and evening of April 12th. Ample 0 to 6 km shear of 60 to 70 kts, combined with MLCAPE values of 1000-2500 J/kg resulted in a prime environment for severe thunderstorms. Severe hail averaging in size from quarters to ping-pong balls fell across portions of southeast South Dakota, southwest Minnesota, and northwest Iowa. Another cold front-induced line of convection developed later in the evening across eastern Nebraska and northwest Iowa, with the primary threat being damaging winds. ||More widespread synoptic high winds followed the passage of a strong cold front. Peak wind gusts in excess of 58 mph occurred across much of southeast South Dakota and into portions of northwest Iowa.

episodes.168401: Thunderstorms developed along a dryline across the Big Country the afternoon of Tuesday April 12, then spread east across North and Central Texas, producing all modes of severe weather. Extremely large hail occurred over parts of our Central Texas counties, where a record-breaking hailstone over 5.6 inches in length was documented in the Salado area of Bell County. This hailstone is now the largest recorded hailstone in our CWA to date. Two tornadoes also occurred across Central Texas in Bell County. An EF-3 tornado started in Williamson County and moved northeast and then northerly across the Salado area. Twenty-three people were injured but no fatalities occurred. Additional storms developed overnight into Wednesday as a cold front pushed through the area, some of which also became severe.
episodes.168461: Melting of the snowpack combined with several episodes of heavier rainfall caused minor flooding on the Sturgeon River in Houghton County during mid-April.
episodes.168507: Heavy rain fell across portions of southeast Minnesota from April 12th into the 13th. Runoff from this rain caused some minor river flooding to occur on the Whitewater River in Whitewater State Park (Olmsted County).
episodes.168767: On the evening of April 13, 2022, a line of severe storms, moving along a cold front, knocked a few trees down in Dubois County.
episodes.168768: On the evening of April 13, 2022, a line of severe storms, moving along a cold front, spawned nine tornadoes as it moved east across Kentucky. One of these was an EF-1 that hit Jefferson County. In addition to tornadoes, strong straight line winds also caused widespread damage across central Kentucky.
episodes.168793: A number of severe storms traversed across the central sections of Kansas on April 12th, 2022. Hail up to golfball size was reported during the early portions of the event however, the size had quickly subsided to around the size of a quarter for most locations.
episodes.169110: A line of severe thunderstorms moved across Middle Tennessee during the late afternoon and evening hours on April 13, 2022. Widespread damaging winds affected most counties of Middle Tennessee, with numerous trees and power lines blown down along with widely scattered structural damage. Winds were measured up to nearly 70 mph.
episodes.169146: On the morning hours of April 13 a decaying MCS moved into the KC Metro, and caused a wind gust of 59 mph at the Downtown Airport in Kansas City.
episodes.170291: A few rounds of severe thunderstorms moved across portions of southeast Arkansas from late in the evening of April 12th through the evening of April 13th. These storms produced wind damage and several tornadoes before a cold front brought an end to storms from west to east.
episodes.170294: A few rounds of severe thunderstorms moved across portions of northeast Louisiana from late in the evening of April 12th through the evening of April 13th. These storms produced wind damage and several tornadoes before a cold front brought an end to storms from west to east.
episodes.170436: A strong and slow moving area of low pressure moved from the Central Plains on the 12th to over Minnesota on the morning of the 14th and became occluded. A cold front pushed across northwest Wisconsin on the 13th with heavy rainfall being received in some locations. Rainfall totals or 2-3 inches were recorded around Washburn County with most falling in a 5 hour period. Additionally, frost was still in the ground leading to higher than normal runoff rates. This lead to isolated minor flooding of ditches along with a few shoulder and road washouts in the Washburn County area. The worst damage was two large culvert pipes that were washed out in Barronett causing damage to a road as well. Additionally, a school bus in Price County tried to drive through a flooded roadway and became stuck as the shoulder gave way underneath it.
episodes.170469: A few rounds of severe thunderstorms moved across portions of Mississippi from late in the evening of April 12th through the evening of April 13th. These storms produced wind damage and several tornadoes before a cold front brought an end to storms from west to east.

An ice jam developed on the Saint John River during the evening of the 12th. Rising water levels in the vicinity of the jam led to flooding and closure along a portion of Route 161 near the Allagash and Saint Francis town line. The road closure was brief...only around 90 minutes...before the ice jam released allowing water levels to recede. The road was re-opened once river levels fell and ice was cleared from the road.

A band of damaging straight line winds estimated between 75-85 mph developed along the leading edge of a quasi-linear convective system (QLCS) across a portion of the Southern Hills neighborhood of South Shreveport, from the parent storm that would later spawn an EF-0 tornado over Southeast Shreveport and South Bossier City only 6-15 minutes later. Multiple large trees were snapped and uprooted in an area bounded by Bert Kouns Industrial loop to the south, Walker Road to the west, Highway 3132 to the north, and Kingston Road to the east. Trees fell on at least four homes in this area, with numerous large limbs snapped as well. A large portion of a metal roof was peeled off of the back of a used car company on Mackey Lane, with numerous shingles removed off of a business in the South Park Village. The front facade of another adjacent business in South Park Village was also blown into the parking lot. All of the snapped and uprooted trees throughout Southern Hills as well as the roof/facade damage in South Park Village were all blown/lying in a north-northeast direction, indicative of straight line winds.
A portion of the roof of RJ's Restaurant was damaged. A sign from the restaurant was blown across Mansfield Road as well.
The report was received via mPING.

An EF-0 tornado with estimated maximum winds around 80 mph which was embedded in a quasi-linear convective system (QLCS) touched down on a farm to the northwest of Blanchard in Caddo Parish. A center pivot irrigation system was flipped by the tornado as it crossed an open field. The tornado then snapped tree limbs before partially removing the roofs of four metal farm buildings along Sentell Road. The tornado then crossed the Red River into Bossier Parish. It should be noted that while the tornado was an EF-0 in Caddo Parish, it did intensify into an EF-1 with estimated maximum winds around 110 mph after it entered Bossier Parish.
COOP Observer reported 1.5 inch hail.
Numerous trees and power lines were downed throughout the city of Shreveport and the surrounding areas.

This is a continuation of the Caddo Parish tornado. This tornado intensified to an EF-1 with estimated maximum winds near 110 mph as it moved over a heavily wooded area near and just south of Willow Bend Road northwest of Benton, where it snapped and uprooted hardwood and softwood trees. The most intense damage was to a guest house which was shifted off of its foundation and destroyed. The tornado continued on to remove a large portion of the roof of a two-story single family home. Two children on the second story of the home were saved by their father who got the Tornado Warning via a Wireless Emergency Alert (WEA) on his wireless phone, and then moved them to a tornado shelter in the center of the home on the first floor. The tornado continued on to damage another single family home and then cross Old Plain Dealing Road. After crossing Old Plain Dealing Road, the tornado removed the roof of a small metal outbuilding and snapped/uprooted several more hardwood and softwood trees before moving into a forested area and lifting.

An EF-0 tornado with estimated maximum winds near 85 mph embedded within a quasi-linear convective system (QLCS) touched down along Sophia Lane and Brunswick Drive in Southeast Shreveport. There, large branches of hardwood and softwood trees were broken and twisted off. The tornado then damaged a food stand as it crossed Youree Drive, while also damaging large branches and uprooting a couple of trees. Minor shingle damage to single family homes adjacent to LSU-Shreveport also resulted from this tornado, before tracking across the LSU-S campus, uprooting trees and downing large branches. The tornado also damaged the soccer and baseball fields at LSU-S before crossing East Kings Highway and the Red River into Western Bossier Parish.

The is a continuation of the Eastern Caddo Parish (Southeast Shreveport) EF-0 tornado. This tornado maintained its intensity with estimated maximum winds near 85 mph as it crossed over into South Bossier City in Bossier Parish, where it continued to uproot trees and down/twist large tree branches. It also uprooted trees which split at least three manufactured homes off of Alfred Lane as they fell and damaged several others. The tornado continued on to General Ewell Drive, and then moved over a forested area on Barksdale Air Force Base. Personnel from Barksdale Air Force Base relayed that trees were uprooted and that large tree branches were broken via pictures as the tornado crossed the southern and eastern forested portions of the base. Beyond Barksdale Air Force Base, only thunderstorm wind damage was found off of Union Texas Road and Academy Lane by Haughton Elementary School in Haughton.

An EF-0 tornado with estimated maximum winds near 80 mph that was embedded within a quasi-linear convective system (QLCS), briefly touched down along Hosston Rodessa Road just north of the Hosston city limits, where it twisted and broke off small and large hardwood tree branches. The tornado continued to down additional tree branches along Christian Street, before lifting as it crossed Highway 71.
Trees were downed at Bossier Elementary School.

A spring storm coupled with frost leaving the ground led to excessive runoff that resulted in damage to two culverts. Pictures show culverts being pushed upward. Protection on the road was necessary due to sinkholes that opened up above the culverts. Both culverts will need replacing. Each culvert is 84 inches by 70 feet with preliminary estimated costs of $20,000 to replace culverts and make repairs to the road along with time and equipment. The Town of Baronett requested an emergency declaration to help cover the costs.
Widespread trees and power lines were blown down across much of Desoto Parish.
A KWCH storm chaser reported numerous dime to nickel sized hailstones on Highway 56.
A tree was blown down on Highway 175 near Mansfield.
Quarter sized hail fell near Ostrander.
Personal weather station sustained at 54 mph and gusted to 75 mph.
Several trees were blown down in and near Doyline.
This was reported on the north side of Hutchinson along with 50 mph winds.
Trees were blown down near the intersection of Old Highway 7 and Marathon Road just southeast of Cotton Valley.
A couple of trees were downed.
Peak gust reported at Webster City Municipal Airport.
This was a measured wind gust.
Nickel sized hail reported.
Trees were blown down on Martha Woods Road near Heflin.

An EF-1 tornado with estimated maximum winds near 100 mph touched down in a wooded area west of Layfield Road west of Castor, and tracked northeast across Highway 4, snapping and uprooting numerous trees along its path. One area of maximum winds was found in an open field just west of Layfield Road where 10-11 wooden power poles were snapped just west of Highway 4. The tornado continued northeast across Highway 792 north of Castor, where it tracked along and just north of Ayers Road and across a logging camp, where a second area of maximum winds were found on Kepler Road just north of Ayers Road. The tornado continued to track northeast over a heavily wooded area inaccessible by vehicle, but dopplar radar indicated a tornadic debris signature north of Highway 4 and west of Highway 9. The tornado lifted prior to reaching Highway 9 and the community of Bienville, although straight line winds estimated to be near 90 mph were found here as numerous trees were snapped and uprooted, but all lying in a northeasterly direction.
Peak gust at Clarion.
Personal weather station gusted to 62 mph.
Multiple trees were blown down in and near Sibley.

This QLCS tornado developed to the southwest of the intersection of 43rd Street SW and South Federal Avenue.  The tornado crossed Federal Avenue and produced EF1 damage to several commercial buildings on the east side of the road.   The tornado continued northeast and damaged another commercial building along 245th Street near the Union Pacific railroad.  Additional damage occurred to trees along S Kentucky Avenue and eventually near 4th Street SE near Yorktown Pike.   The tornado lifted before encountering Buena Vista University - Mason City Campus.
Several trees were blown down across the city of Minden, with some trees falling on vehicles.
Multiple trees were blown down in and near Dubberly.

Tornado developed south of Highway 9 and west of Warbler Avenue and moved northeast.  The tornado encountered a farmstead on the south side of Highway 9 producing EF1 damage to trees and an outbuilding.  The tornado continued northeast and remained in rural farmland the rest of its path.
A 66 mph wind gust was measured at the Minden Airport.

An EF-0 tornado with estimated maximum winds near 85 mph briefly touched down on the west side of Highway 371 about one mile south of Prescott, where a number of trees were uprooted. The tornado crossed Highway 371 where additional trees were uprooted, before the tornado lifted.
An EF0 tornado developed northeast of Nora Springs and moved northeast across rural parts of Floyd County before moving into Mitchell County. Damage appeared to be limited and mainly to trees.
Trees were blown down and a camper destroyed on the northwest side of Austin.
Quarter sized hail was reported in Taopi.
Trees were knocked down.

This EF2 tornado formed southwest of Taopi and quickly intensified and caused significant damage in Taopi. Most buildings were damaged and 10 were destroyed. Cars were tossed, grain bins destroyed, and numerous trees and power lines downed. Two people were injured seeking shelter from the storm when they became trapped under debris. Just outside of Taopi, part of the roof was removed from a farmhouse, several outbuildings were damaged, and several head of cattle were missing.

This EF0 tornado developed in Floyd County and moved into Mitchell County southwest of Osage. The tornado moved to the northeast across rural parts of southern Mitchell County before dissipating south of Osage. Damage was primarily limited to trees.
Eight trees were downed along FM 227.
Some large trees were snapped and a nearby house sustained minor roof and siding damage north of Taopi.
An estimated 60 mph wind gust occurred at the fire station in Charles City.

This EF1 tornado developed southwest of Brownville and proceeded to move northeast through the small community before dissipating northeast of town. Farm outbuildings and trees were damaged along the path.

This EF1 tornado developed south of New Haven and tracked northeast before moving into Howard County, passing south of Riceville. Along the path, numerous farm buildings, grain bins, and trees were damaged or destroyed.

A wide swath of mainly tree damage occurred in Southeast Claiborne Parish several miles east southeast of Lisbon, particularly along Highway 152, Revis Fowler Road, Kimbletown Road, and Wilson Road south of Highway 2. Numerous trees were snapped and uprooted across these areas, with a metal canopy tossed adjacent to the intersection of Highway 152 and Kimbletown Road.
The automated weather observing equipment at the Charles City airport measured a 64 mph gust.
This EF1 tornado moved into Howard County south of Riceville and moved to the northeast before dissipating southeast of Riceville. Damage was mainly limited to trees.
A section of metal roofing was blown off a large farm outbuilding southwest of Spring Valley.

An EF1 tornado formed southwest of Spring Valley and moved almost due north before dissipating west of Spring Valley. The tornado blew down a barn and damaged several other farm buildings along its path. Several new power poles along County Highway 1 were leaning after the storm.
Power poles were blown down in Spring Valley from an estimated 60 mph gust. A pavillion was destroyed in a city park and the high school sustained some damage.
An EF0 tornado developed southwest of Saratoga and tracked to the northeast before dissipating southeast of town. The tornado damaged trees and some farm outbuildings along its path.
A farm outbuilding had the roof and one wall blown off near Spring Valley.
The roof was blown off a farm outbuilding with a section of metal roofing taken off another and trees were snapped off northeast of Spring Valley.
A half dozen campers were tipped over at a campground northeast of Preston.
A power pole was snapped and power lines were downed across from the Calhoun Fire Department station on Cowboy Road in Calhoun.
A large tree was blown down across Claiborne Road in the Calhoun area.
A tree fell onto a mobile home in the Truxno community.
Trees were uprooted near Calhoun at Exit 103 on I-20. A nearby power pole was snapped. A tree fell on a car at this same location.
Outbuildings were damaged along with trees and power lines blown down southwest of Lewiston. Parts of the downed trees landed on a house.

An EF0 tornado touched down just outside of Ridgeway and moved into the very northwest side of town before dissipating. A few farm outbuildings were damaged along the path, and a livestock trailer was flipped onto its top.
A farm outbuilding had the roof and two walls blown off southwest of Ridgeway.
Some outbuildings were damaged in Ridgeway.
At the high school in Lewiston, metal bleachers were ripped off the main seating area, smaller metal bleachers were blown across the track and part of the track was ripped up.
A tree was blown down onto a home on Park Avenue in Monroe.
This EF0 tornado moved across rural parts of southwest Winona County in the Shelton Hill area. The tornado only caused some tree damage as it moved across farm fields.
An old garage was pushed over by winds northeast of Ridgeway.
An estimated 62 mph gust occurred in Bluffton.
This EF0 tornado developed just southeast of the Fremont area in southwest Winona County and moved north across Interstate 90 before dissipating. Damage was limited to trees.
A large farm outbuilding had part of the roof and walls blown off east of Ridgeway.
A tree and a power pole were downed near Bon Aire Drive and Old Sterlington Road in Monroe.
A power outage was caused by downed tree branches north of Wilson.
A farm outbuilding was damaged north of Fremont.
Trees and power lines were damaged just west of Winona.

A large tree was blown down on CR 2041 near Appleby.
Quarter size hail fell on the southwest side of Nacogdoches.
Quarter size hail was reported in Nacogdoches.
Pearl Street was flooded in Nacogdoches.

Lightning struck a home along LA Highway 589, and the home burned down.
A tree was blown down along LA Highway 879 near its intersection with Cook Road.
Power poles were blown down on Willie Herron Road.
The roof was blown off a barn near Tomah.
High water covered Highway 7 just outside of the Center city limits.
High water covered Highway 7 about 6 miles southwest of Center.
Several power poles were broken, some trees were blown down, and three homes were damaged by wind along US Highway 82 and in the Lakehall Road area.
A few trees were blown down in the Glen Allan community.
ASOS measured 59 mph wind gusts.

A line of severe storms caused some wind damage between Greenville and Wayside, including a tree blown down on Glendale Road and trees and power lines blown down near the intersection of Mississippi Highways 1 and 438.
Runoff after a heavy rain event pushed the Whitewater River out of its banks in the Whitewater State Park. The river crested almost a foot above flood stage at 14.3 feet.
A few power poles were blown down along LA Highway 128.
A shed was damaged along LA Highway 606.
A tree was blown down onto a power line near the intersection of Old Fannin Road and Eagle Drive.
Quarter size hail fell on the southeast side of Dubberly.
Golf ball size hail was measured in the Taylor community.
Trees and power lines were blown down near the intersection of US Highway 41 and Monticello Road.
A gas station canopy at the intersection of US Highway 51 and Factory Street was damaged.
Mobile homes were damaged in the Pisgah community.
US 167 on the north side of Bernice was closed in both directions due to downed power lines lying across the road.
Multiple trees and power lines were downed on Highway 2 West from the Bernice Elementary School, forcing the closure of the roadway.
Roofs were damaged to mobile homes and other buildings in Bernice. Numerous trees were blown down as well.
Multiple trees and power lines were downed on Pleasant Hill Road between Spearsville and Farmerville.
Golf ball size hail broke windows and damaged siding to a home on Lockwood Road.
Numerous trees and power lines were downed several miles northwest of Farmerville.
Multiple trees were downed in the Truxno community.
The Mesonet Station FW2066 in Camdenton reported a three hour precipitation total of 1.27 inches.
The Mesonet station FW9035 in Cassville recorded a three hour precipitation total of 1.20 inches.
River entered flood state at 515am LST on the 13th of April, crested at 10.91 ft at 745am LST on April 13th, and fell below flood stage at 645pm LST on April 13th.

A school bus became stranded in flood waters when the shoulder washed out underneath it and it partially tipped. Four students and the driver were helped from the bus to safety and there were no injuries reported, although the bus driver was taken to the hospital to be checked out. The bus went through the flooded section of road 15 minutes prior to returning and trying to make it through a second time.
A photograph on social media indicated quarter sized hail in Van Alstyne, TX.
The Mesonet Station DW7816 three miles SW of Rogersville reported a three hour rainfall total of 1.14 inches.
Penny sized hail was reported.
Emergency management reported quarter sized hail in Dodd City, TX.
A public report indicated dime sized hail about 6 miles north-northwest of Hutchins, TX.
A social media report indicated quarter sized hail about 2 miles east of Royse City, TX.
Hail was up to nickel size for about five minutes.

This tornado developed south of the E 820 Road and west of the S 4700 Road, where large tree limbs were snapped and homes were damaged. It moved east-northeast across the cemetery snapping softwood trees. The tornado then moved across the northwest and north sides of Stilwell, where the roofs of a number of apartment buildings were damaged, homes were damaged, outbuildings were destroyed, trees were uprooted, and power poles were blown down. Several businesses were damaged as it crossed Highway 59, a semi truck was blown over, and trees were uprooted. As the tornado moved east-northeast from Stilwell, numerous trees were uprooted, outbuildings were damaged, and some trees and power poles were snapped from the S 4720 Road to near the S 4757 Road. The tornado appeared to dissipate just east of the S 4757 road. Based on this damage, maximum estimated wind in the tornado was 95 to 105 mph.
The combination of heavy rain and snowmelt resulted in minor flooding along the Sturgeon River near Alston.

A shallow vortex, known as a gustnado, developed along the leading edge of thunderstorm outflow and damaged the roof of a church, snapped large tree limbs, and blew down a power pole. This vortex was recorded by a security camera.
Portions of Country Club Drive were reported flooded and closed.
Portions of several roads were flooded, and flood water entered a business.
Portions of Sleepy Hollow Road were flooded southwest of Gentry.
The Branson Mesonet Station FW9611 measured a 61mph wind gust.
Several trees were downed just southwest of Mount Vernon.
Portions of numerous roads were flooded and closed across the county. There was at least one swift water rescue performed for a stranded motorist.
Several trees were downed in Avery.
A one-mile section of Highway 12 was flooded and closed in both directions.
Missouri Highway 76 was closed to traffic east of MO-112 due to flooding.
A half-mile section of Highway 16 was flooded and closed in both directions, and a section of Highway 412 was flooded and closed in both directions.
Several trees and power lines were blown down in Mount Pleasant.
A home lost several soffit panels and a chicken coop was damaged.
Several large limbs were downed and a few trees were uprooted in town. No property damage was reported.

Multiple hardwood and softwood trees and power poles were snapped across portions of the Malta community, with more isolated uprooted trees observed across FM 2789 and CR 3103. The westward facing portion of a metal roof on a single family home was blown off into pieces landing to the east around a tree and across CR 3103.
Highway C at Flat Creek was flooded and impassable.
Highway O at Tory Creek was flooded and impassable.
Several trees and large limbs were downed southeast of Foreman.
High winds downed a tree onto a powerline causing a power outage.
Highway 14 at Cowskin Creek was flooded and impassable.
Standing water was reported on several streets in Harrison.

Heavy rain fell over Roaring River State Park causing Roaring River to flood campgrounds 2, 3 and the lower loop of campground 1. Thirty two campers were evacuated prior to the peak flooding.  Minor damage to the park was reported as a result of the fast moving water.
Highway 5 at Bryant Creek was flooded and impassable.
Wester Bluff Road and Panther Creek road were flooded and impassable along Panther Creek.
Highway KK at Panther Creek was flooded and impassable.
Highway FF at Hunter Creek was flooded and impassable with over 2 feet of water.
Several roads were flooded near Harmony.
Reports were received of damage to powerlines between Bonnerdale and Pearcy from thunderstorms that moved through earlier in the day.
A trained spotter reported quarter sized hail in Celeste, TX.
Highway Y at Cowskin Creek was flooded and impassable.
A public report indicated dime sized hail in Fate, TX.
Three inch tree limbs were snapped in Hope. Power poles were also broken in this area.
Reports were received of a water rescue after a car was swept away at the intersection of 3rd Street and Park Street in Flippin.
The local coordinator reported just over 2000 residents without power as a result of severe weather.
Portions of several roads were flooded by heavy rainfall.
Trees were blown down a couple miles northeast of Hope.
Broadcast media reported quarter sized hail about 2 miles north of Greenville, TX.
A public report indicated quarter sized hail about 3 miles west of Campbell, TX.
Multiple people camping on a gravel bar near Farm Road 2265 were rescued as Roaring River rose rapidly due to heavy rainfall. All individuals were rescued safely.
A public report indicated quarter sized hail about a mile west-southwest of Commerce, TX.
Powerlines were reported downed by thunderstorm winds near the town of Lono, along Hwy. 222.
Entergy reported powerlines were downed due to thunderstorm winds about 2 miles north of Malvern near I-40 and east Butterfield-Cutoff Rd.
Route AB was closed at a low water area due to flooding.
Law enforcement reported quarter to golf ball sized hail in Cumby, TX.
Power outages were reported off Springhill Rd. in Bryant due to thunderstorm winds.
A report was received of trees down near the Little Rock Zoo.

An ice jam on the Little Black River produced minor flooding along portions of Walker Brook Road...Rapid Road and Little Black Road. The flooding also impacted several homes and structures along the river.
Reports were received of power outages in Ward, Austin, and parts of Cabot.
Trees and power lines were reported down in Park Hill and North Hills.
A trained spotter reported quarter sized hail about 2 miles east-southeast of Enchanted Oaks, TX.
A tree was down near the intersection of McCain Blvd. and North Hills Blvd., blocking traffic.
Highway Z at Elk Creek was flooded and impassable.
Tory Creek Road along Tory Creek was flooded and impassable.
A trained spotter reported ping pong ball sized hail in Malakoff, TX.
A public report indicated ping pong ball sized hail about a mile east-southeast of Malakoff, TX.
A trained spotter reported nickel sized hail about a mile east-southeast of Streetman, TX.
A public report indicated quarter sized hail about 4 miles west-southwest of Athens, TX.
Tree limbs were snapped and trees were uprooted on C Street in the Hillcrest part of Little Rock.
Trees and power lines were downed in Omaha.
Highway U at Bryant Creek was flooded and impassable.
Trees were down on Elm St. in the Hillcrest area of Little Rock.
Flooding was reported in the high school, along with portions of U.S. Hwy. 167.
The Lawrence county OEM reported power lines downed in Walnut Ridge. The Lawrence county AWOS recorded a peak wind gust of 44 mph about the same time as the report.
Highway EE at the North Fork River was flooded and impassable.
Trees were downed in Lone Star.
Trees and power lines were downed on the west side of Texarkana.
County Road 519 was washed out at Prairie Creek due to high flood water.
Measured thunderstorm wind gust of 66 mph by the Jonesboro ASOS.

This tornado began near County Road 963 east-southeast of Brookland, damaging trees as it moved east-northeast across Ditch Levee Road. Several wooden, high-tension power poles were down southwest of the intersection of Brookland School Road East and Bowman Road. A home also sustained roof damage near this intersection. More substantial damage was seen in the Dixie community where several structures sustained roof damage and trees were uprooted. The tornado continued to move northeast, ending just past County Road 999. Peak winds were estimated at 100 mph. Thanks to NSSL for assistance with this damage survey.
Tree blown down crossing both lanes of Highway 463.
Wires down near the high school.
Barn damaged and power lines down near Highway 135 and Greene County Road 960.
Numerous powerlines down near Schugtown in Eastern Craighead County.
Damage to roof of new building at Main Street and Highway 412.
Measured gust of 60 mph by the Missouri Mesonet Station.
Trees uprooted and power lines down in Cardwell Area.

This tornado began just south of West County Road 70 in the Garson area causing damage to hardwood trees. As the tornado moved northeast across agricultural land, several center pivot irrigation systems were rolled. The tornado crossed into Dunklin County near County Road 645, damaging a mobile home unit and additional center pivot irrigation systems along Missouri Route K and County Road 626. An outbuilding was damaged along County Road 655 with the tornado lifting as it moved into Hornersville. Thanks to NSSL for assistance with this damage survey.
A public report indicated dime sized hail about 4 miles northeast of Palestine, TX.

This tornado began just south of County Road West County Road 70 in the Garson area causing damage to hardwood trees. As the tornado moved northeast across agricultural land, several center pivot irrigation systems were rolled. The tornado crossed into Dunklin County near County Road 645, damaging a mobile home unit and additional center pivot irrigation systems along Missouri Route K and County Road 626. An outbuilding was damaged along County Road 655 with the tornado lifting as it moved into Hornersville. Peak winds were estimated at 85 mph. Thanks to NSSL for assistance with this damage survey.
A public report indicated dime sized hail about 3 miles southeast of Palestine, TX.
House damaged.
Utility pole knocked down along Highway 1 south of Forrest City.
Power poles down on Highway 14 at Mississippi/Poinsett County line.
Highway Z at the Finley Creek was flooded and impassable.

The tornado began near Highway 140 and West County Road 738 in the West Ridge community. A metal building and a home sustained minor damage and much of the roof was removed from the old school building on Highway 297 just east of Highway 140. The tornado continued northeast, depositing debris in the field downstream of the school, eventually crossing the intersection of Highways 140 and 136 on the east side of Three Way. Minor roof and tree damage was observed here with the tornado quickly lifting. Peak winds were estimated at 80 mph. Thanks to NSSL for assistance with this damage survey.
Heavy rainfall produced street flooding.

A vehicle driven into a flooded low water crossing near the intersection of county roads 705 and 741 was swept away, with the driver drowning in the flood water. Heavy rainfall had ended by early afternoon, but some low water crossings remained flooded well after the rain had stopped.
Trees were uprooted.
Several trees were reported down approximately 6 miles south of Brinkley.

An irrigation pivot was overturned.

Lightning destroyed home in Newcastle community north of Forrest City. The home was a total loss.
Flooding was reported over portions of Boone Rd. and Meadowbrook St.
Power poles snapped on I-55 between Wardell and Hayward exits.
Highway 142 at Bennetts River was flooded and impassable.
Powerlines were blown down by thunderstorm winds.
A report was received via mPING of a car stalled in water on Hwy. 70 near East Washington Rd.
Broadcast media tweeted a photo of deep water running over a road in Alexander.
The intersection of West Maple and N. Main St. was flooded with approximately one foot of water.
Several trees were downed along Highway 79.
A couple of trees were down near the intersection of Highways 166 and 116.

Tree knocked down next to a home on Curve Nankipoo Road.

Multiple trees down on a couple of houses.

Several farm outbuildings sustained partial or complete loss of metal roofing. A carport was damaged. Some trees were down. Peak winds were estimated around 80 mph.

Photos shared on social media showed a semi truck blown over, northward on Wilmington Road, west of Route 45.
Trees damaged along Milltown Road.

An EF-1 tornado began south of Eagle Lake in Warren County near Mississippi Highway 465, where it snapped numerous trees. The tornado continued east into Issaquena County where it continued to snap and uproot numerous trees. The tornado continued back into Warren County near MS Highway 465. It continued to snap and uproot numerous trees along its path, and then it dissipated just east of US Highway 61. The estimated peak wind gust was 105 mph. The total path length was 10.1 miles across both counties.

The intersection of Arkansas 1 and US Highway 79 flooded with approximately 12 to 16 inches of water.
A downed tree blocked Highway 641 in Benton. Just southeast of Benton, a tree was down on a house and power lines. A house roof was damaged 5 miles northeast of Benton.

An EF-1 tornado bean south of MS Highway 3 on the northeast side of Redwood and moved northeast. It snapped and uprooted numerous trees along its short track, including several near the International Paper Plant. The tornado dissipated after crossing Highway 3 on the east side of the paper plant. The estimated peak wind gust was 95 mph.

The tornado formed southwest of Hematite Lake in the Land Between The Lakes National Recreation Area. It crossed just south of the Woodlands Nature Station and then across Lake Barkley into Lyon County. Many tree limbs were blown down. Multiple large trees were uprooted. Peak winds were estimated near 95 mph.
Northbound lanes of Highway 51 between Atoka and Brighton closed due to flooding.
The siding of a house was damaged. A porch roof was damaged. A small chicken coop was destroyed, and a barn roof was blown off. A few trees were damaged. Peak winds were estimated near 85 mph.

This tornado crossed from Trigg County into Lyon County. Much of the Lyon County portion of the path was over Lake Barkley. On the Lyon County shore, a tree and some branches were blown down in a subdivision. Peak winds were estimated near 95 mph.

A brief tornado touched down in the Dixie Farm Road area outside of Satartia north of Mississippi Highway 3. A tornadic debris signature was observed with this tornado on radar, and law enforcement witnessed a funnel cloud. Much of the of area was open farm land, and where potential tree damage may have occurred was not accessible. Due to this, the rating was assigned as EFU.

An EF-1 tornado with estimated maximum winds near 100 mph touched down in a heavily wooded area just west of Highway 127 southeast of Sikes in Northeast Winn Parish, where it snapped and uprooted numerous trees. This tornado tracked northeast across another heavily wooded area northeast of Highway 127, which was inaccessible by vehicle. However, the Fort Polk dopplar radar indicated a tornadic debris signature northeast of Highway 127 near the Caldwell Parish line, with the tornado continuing east-northeast into Western Caldwell Parish before intensifying into a low end EF-2 with estimated maximum winds near 115 mph on the Enhanced Fujita Scale.
Tunica AWOS measured a wind gust of 70 mph.
Trees fell on multiple homes in Eudora, damaging one roof.

The is a continuation of the Northeast Winn Parish tornado. This tornado intensified to an EF-2 on the Enhanced Fujita Scale with estimated maximum winds around 115 mph shortly after entering Western Caldwell Parish in an area that remained inaccessible by vehicle. However, the Fort Polk dopplar radar continued to indicate a tornadic debris signature as the tornado tracked across Childress Road where the strongest winds were observed. Numerous trees were snapped and uprooted, with a couple falling onto homes in this area. Remarkedly, most of the homes avoided significant damage, as the densely wooded area shielded the higher winds from these homes. The tornado continued northeast across Highway 126 and Wiles Road, where numerous trees were snapped and uprooted. Again, several homes were protected from these trees with little if any damage, where the tornado reached its widest point along Wiles Road and as it crossed Highway 4 west of Columbia. Numerous trees were uprooted in front of a residence opposite of the intersection of Highway 3239, with the tornado continuing northeast and finally lifting northwest of Columbia before reaching Highway 165 between Columbia and Riverton. These storms then transitioned into a damaging straight line wind event as several large tree limbs were snapped along both sides of Highway 165, with additional straight line wind damage noted along Highway 133 in the Hebert community along the Caldwell/Richland Parish line. Several trees were uprooted and large limbs were snapped in this area. However, the tree debris here all were lying in a southeasterly direction. In all, this tornado remained on the ground for approximately 19.3 miles from Northwest Winn into Central Caldwell Parish.

An EF-0 tornado touched down near Hole 1 on the Refuge golf course, where it blew a tree down, and then moved east across Airport Road. Another tree was blown down near the road. A very narrow and intermittent condensation funnel could be seen from the NWS Jackson Forecast Office as it moved across the Jackson - Medgar Wiley Evers airfield. The tornado appeared to broaden and become more easily visible as it moved to the eastern side of the airfield, with several storm chaser reports and videos showing development as the tornado moved across East Metro Parkway and the forested area between there and Cooper Road. Scattered small tree limbs were blown down where the tornado crossed East Metro Parkway and also near the intersection of Cooper Road and Dogwood Place where the tornado dissipated. The estimated peak wind gust was 70 mph.
